1.note: Isaiah is speaking of Zion as if it were a living thing that could **Arise** and **shine**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Wake up and shine]

The words **you** and **your** and the implied “you” in imperatives are feminine singular here and throughout this chapter because Yahweh is addressing Zion, personified as a woman. So use singular forms in your translation if your language marks that distinction, and use feminine forms if your language marks that distinction.

Here Yahweh is speaking as if the deliverance and glory coming to Jerusalem were a **light** that had come to it. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [your deliverance has come]

Here Yahweh is speaking as if his **glory** were the sun that **has risen upon** Jerusalem. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and Yahweh is now revealing his glory to you]

2.note: Here Yahweh is speaking as if **darkness** and **gloom** were physical coverings that would spread over the earth and its peoples. He means that trouble and the absence of his favor will characterize the nations. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the earth will experience trouble, and the peoples will lack Yahweh’s favor]

Isaiah is using the term **behold** to focus his listeners’ attention on what he is about to say. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation. Alternate translation: [Now look]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **darkness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [dark things]

Yahweh is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [and gloom will cover the peoples]

Here Yahweh is speaking as if he himself were the sun that would **rise upon** Jerusalem. He means that he will appear to his people and shine his favor on them. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [but Yahweh will appear to you and show you his favor]

The expression **will be seen** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [and people will see his glory upon you]

3.q: וְ⁠הָלְכ֥וּ גוֹיִ֖ם לְ⁠אוֹרֵ֑⁠ךְ וּ⁠מְלָכִ֖ים לְ⁠נֹ֥גַהּ זַרְחֵֽ⁠ךְ
3.note: These two clauses mean basically the same thing. The second emphasizes the meaning of the first by repeating the same idea with different words. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could combine them and express the emphasis in another way. Alternate translation: [And even kings of the nations will come to your bright light]

Here Yahweh is speaking as if the restored glory of Jerusalem were a **light** that the nations would travel toward. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And nations will travel toward the light of your renewed glory]

Yahweh is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [and kings will go to the brightness of your rising]

If your language does not use abstract nouns for the ideas of **brightness** and **rising**, you could express the same ideas in other ways. Alternate translation: [to how brightly you shine as you rise]

4.note: Yahweh is using **Lift up your eyes** as a common expression to mean “look around.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Direct your gaze]

The pronouns **them** and **they** refer to the people who belong to Jerusalem and are returning to it, that is, the sons and daughters mentioned next. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [all of your people gather themselves, they come to you]

Here Yahweh is speaking of the people who belong to Jerusalem as if they were the city’s **sons** and **daughters**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [The men who belong to you will come from faraway, and the women who belong to you]

The expression **will be supported** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [and people will support your daughters on the side]

The implication is that the young daughters will be carried on the hip, as adults carry small children. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [will be carried on the hip like small children]

5.note: Here Yahweh is speaking as if Jerusalem would physically shine, or **be radiant**, when he means that its people will glow with joy. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and be filled with joy]

Here Yahweh is speaking as if the **heart** of Jerusalem’s people would grow wider. He means that they will be overwhelmed with wonder and joy. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and your heart will thrill and be filled with wonder and joy]

Here, **the abundance of the sea** represents the great wealth that traders will bring to Jerusalem from lands across the sea. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the great wealth from lands across the sea]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **abundance**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the abundant goods coming by sea]

The expression **will be turned** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [the sea will turn its abundance to you]

6.note: Yahweh says that **A multitude of camels will cover you** as an extreme statement for emphasis. He means that a very great number of camels will come. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use a different way to express the emphasis. Alternate translation: [So many camels will come to you that they will seem to fill your land]
The word **Ephah** is the name of a region.

Here, the phrase **the praises of Yahweh** uses the possessive form to indicate the one who is praised: the people will praise Yahweh. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [and they will proclaim praises to Yahweh]

7.note: The expression **will be gathered** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [People will gather all of the flocks of Kedar to you]
The word **Nebaioth** is the name of a people group.

The implication is that these flocks and rams will be offered as sacrifices on Yahweh’s altar. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [They will be offered as acceptable sacrifices on my altar]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **acceptance**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [and I will accept them]

Here Yahweh is speaking of his temple as if it were a **house** in which he lived. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and I will glorify my splendid temple]

Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe a **house** that is characterized by **splendor**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [and I will glorify my splendid house]

8.note: Yahweh is using the question form to express wonder at the ships coming swiftly like clouds and doves. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [How marvelous are these ones!]

The point of this comparison is that just as **a cloud** moves swiftly across the sky, so the ships move swiftly toward Jerusalem. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [They move swiftly, like a cloud moving across the sky]

Yahweh is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [and they fly like doves fly to their coops]

The point of this comparison is that just as **doves** fly quickly home to **their coops**, so the exiles hurry home to Jerusalem. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [and they hurry home as quickly as doves flying to their coops]

9.note: Yahweh is speaking of the **coastlands** as if they were people who could **wait for** him. He means that the people who live in those distant lands are eager to do what he commands. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the people of the coastlands eagerly await my command]

The implication is that the **ships of Tarshish** were large seagoing vessels able to travel great distances. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [and the large seagoing ships will be first]

9.q: לְ⁠שֵׁם֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהַ֔יִ⁠ךְ וְ⁠לִ⁠קְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל כִּ֥י פֵאֲרָֽ⁠ךְ
9.note: Even though Yahweh is the one speaking here, he refers to himself in the third person, as **Yahweh your God** and the **Holy One of Israel**, saying that **he has glorified you**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate this in the first person. Alternate translation: [for my name, since I am Yahweh your God and for me, the Holy One of Israel, for I have glorified you]

Here, **the name of Yahweh** represents Yahweh himself and his honor. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [for the honor of Yahweh your God]

10.note: Yahweh uses the word **but** here to indicate a contrast between the punishment he brought in his wrath and the compassion he will show in his favor. In your translation, indicate this contrast in a way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [although in my wrath I struck you, in my favor I will now have compassion on you]

Yahweh is using **sons of foreignness** as a common expression to mean “foreigners.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [foreign peoples]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **foreignness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [people from foreign lands]

The implication is that when Yahweh **struck** Jerusalem, he punished its people by allowing their enemies to defeat them. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [in my wrath I punished you by letting your enemies defeat you]

11.note: The expression **will not be shut** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [day and night no one will shut them]

Yahweh is referring to “all of the time” by naming its two major parts, **day** and **night**. He means that the gates will stay open continually. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [all the time]

Isaiah is emphasizing a positive meaning by using a negative word, **not**, together with a mild expression, **be shut**, that is the opposite of the intended meaning. If it would be helpful in your language, you could emphasize the positive meaning in a strong way. Alternate translation: [they will remain wide open]

The expression **being led** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [with people leading them]

Isaiah assumes that the Israelites, personified as Zion, will know that these **kings** are **being led** to them as prisoners who will acknowledge the Israelites as their rulers. You could say that explicitly if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [being led as prisoners] or [with people leading them as prisoners]

12.note: For the word translated as **For** indicates that what follows is a reason for what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a reason for what came before. Alternate translation: [This is because]

Yahweh is not referring to a specific **nation** or **kingdom**. He means any nation or kingdom that refuses to serve Jerusalem. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [any nation and any kingdom that does not serve you]

The terms **the nation** and **the kingdom** mean similar things. Yahweh is using the two terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [the people group]

Yahweh is repeating forms of the verb **destroy** in order to intensify his expression of the idea that it conveys. If your language can repeat words for intensification, it would be appropriate to do that here in your translation. If not, your language may have another way of expressing the intensification. Alternate translation: [and nations, they will completely destroy]

Yahweh is using the pronoun they in a general sense, not to refer to specific people. Use an expression for this that would be natural in your language. Alternate translation: [yes, those nations will be completely destroyed]

13.note: Here, **The glory of Lebanon** represents the magnificent trees that grew in Lebanon, which the following words name. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [The magnificent trees of Lebanon]

Here Yahweh is speaking of his temple as if it were the **place of** his **feet**, that is, a footstool where he rests his feet. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and I will glorify the place where I rest]

14.note: Here Yahweh is speaking of the descendants of Jerusalem’s oppressors as if they were their **sons**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the descendants of the ones having humbled you]

14.q: וְ⁠הִֽשְׁתַּחֲו֛וּ עַל כַּפּ֥וֹת רַגְלַ֖יִ⁠ךְ כָּל מְנַֽאֲצָ֑יִ⁠ךְ
14.note: Prostrating themselves at the soles of someone’s feet was a symbolic action by which people showed complete submission and respect. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could explain the significance of this action in the text of your translation or in a footnote. Alternate translation: [and all of the ones having despised you will bow low at the soles of your feet to show their complete submission to you]

15.note: The expression **being abandoned and hated** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [people abandoning and hating you]

Yahweh is using **generation and generation** as a common expression to mean “all future generations,” that is, forever. If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [all future generations]

16.q: וְ⁠יָנַקְתְּ֙ חֲלֵ֣ב גּוֹיִ֔ם וְ⁠שֹׁ֥ד מְלָכִ֖ים תִּינָ֑קִי
16.note: Here Yahweh is speaking as if Jerusalem were an infant who would **suck the milk of the nations** and feed at **the breast of kings**. He means that its people will receive the wealth and resources of those nations and their kings. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And you will receive the wealth of the nations, and you will be provided for by their kings]

The terms **Savior** and **Redeemer** mean similar things. Yahweh is using the two terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [am the one who completely rescues you] or [am the one who saves and redeems you]

Here, **Jacob** represents his descendants, the people of Israel. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the Mighty One of the people of Israel]

17.q: וְ⁠תַ֤חַת הָֽ⁠עֵצִים֙ נְחֹ֔שֶׁת וְ⁠תַ֥חַת הָ⁠אֲבָנִ֖ים בַּרְזֶ֑ל
17.note: Yahweh is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [and instead of wood, I will bring bronze, and instead of stones, I will bring iron]

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **peace**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [And I will appoint those who are peaceful as your governor and those who are righteous as your rulers]

Yahweh is speaking of **peace** and **righteousness** as if they were living rulers who could govern Jerusalem. He means that its leaders will govern peacefully and rule justly. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [governors who rule you peacefully and rulers who act righteously]

18.note: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **Violence**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [Violent actions]

The expression **will no longer be heard** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [No one will hear of violence anymore]

Yahweh is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [destruction and breaking will no longer happen within your borders]

The terms **destruction** and **breaking** mean similar things. Yahweh is using the two terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [terrible destruction]

Here Yahweh is speaking as if the walls and gates of Jerusalem could bear the names **Salvation** and **Praise**. He means that the city will be so secure that its walls testify to his saving of it, and people passing through its gates will praise him. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And your walls will show that I have saved the city, and those who pass through your gates will praise me]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **Salvation**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [Yahweh Saves You]

19.q: לֹא יִֽהְיֶה לָּ֨⁠ךְ ע֤וֹד הַ⁠שֶּׁ֨מֶשׁ֙ לְ⁠א֣וֹר יוֹמָ֔ם וּ⁠לְ⁠נֹ֕גַהּ הַ⁠יָּרֵ֖חַ לֹא יָאִ֣יר לָ֑⁠ךְ
19.note: The implication is not that the sun and moon will cease to exist, but that Jerusalem will no longer need them because Yahweh’s presence will give it light. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [You will no longer need the sun for light by day, and you will not need the moon to give you light for brightness]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **eternity**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [for a light that will shine forever]

Here Yahweh is speaking of himself as if he were an everlasting **light** for Jerusalem. He means that his presence will guide his people and give them glory forever. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [but Yahweh will be to you the one who guides you forever]

Yahweh is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [and your God will be to you for your splendor]

20.note: Yahweh is using **Your sun will no longer go in** as a common expression to mean that the sun will no longer set. If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Your sun will no longer set]

Yahweh is using **your moon will not be assembled** as a common expression to mean that the moon will no longer wane, disappear or reappear. If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and your moon will no longer wane]

The expression **will not be assembled** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [and your moon will not gather itself in]

21.note: In this verse, the word **people** is singular in form, but it refers to all the inhabitants of Jerusalem as a group. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use the plural form of “people.” Alternate translation: [And the people of your nation, all of them]

Here Yahweh is speaking of his people as if they were a **branch** that he himself had planted. He means that he established them and caused them to flourish. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the people whom I have established]

Yahweh is using **my hands** to represent himself as the one who acts. He means that his people are the work that he himself has done. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression from your culture or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the work that I have done]

The expression **may be glorified** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [that I may show my glory]

22.q: הַ⁠קָּטֹן֙ יִֽהְיֶ֣ה לָ⁠אֶ֔לֶף וְ⁠הַ⁠צָּעִ֖יר לְ⁠ג֣וֹי עָצ֑וּם
22.note: Yahweh is using the adjectives **small** and **little** as nouns to mean a group of people that is few in number. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate this adjective with an equivalent phrase. Alternate translation: [The small group will become a thousand, and the little group, a strong nation.]

22.q: הַ⁠קָּטֹן֙ יִֽהְיֶ֣ה לָ⁠אֶ֔לֶף וְ⁠הַ⁠צָּעִ֖יר לְ⁠ג֣וֹי עָצ֑וּם
22.note: The terms **The small** and the little mean similar things. Isaiah is using the two terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [Even the smallest, most insignificant group of people will grow large and become a strong nation]

Yahweh is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [and the little group will become a strong nation]

The pronoun **it** refers to everything that Yahweh has promised to do in this chapter. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [will hasten to fulfill these promises in their time]
